Privacy, in plain language

Your work is
not our content.

This demo stores data only in your browser. It has no backend, account server, analytics service, or payment processor.

Activity timing only. Always.

PULSE is designed to understand when you are active or idle—not what you are doing.

What is tracked

  • Session start, pause, and stop times
  • Active and idle duration, stored separately
  • Your selected project or task label
  • Your Productive, Neutral, or Distracting tag
  • Voluntary mood, stress, workload, and comment responses

What is never tracked

  • Keystrokes or what you type
  • Screen content, screenshots, or recordings
  • URLs, browsing history, or document names
  • Passwords, personal files, or webcam/microphone data

What managers can see

Managers see only aggregated team averages, participation rates, trends, and risk indicators. Any team with fewer than five pulse responses is hidden. Individual pulse comments and personal activity timelines are not included in manager views.

Where demo data lives

Timer state, preferences, trial status, and pulse submission state use your browser’s localStorage. They do not sync across devices. Clearing browser data or choosing “Reset demo data” removes them. The demo payment form validates card formatting locally and never transmits or stores a full card number.

Production handoff

The mock async service layer is designed to be replaced by a real backend. A production implementation should add encryption, access controls, retention policies, consent management, and a formal privacy review before collecting real employee data.
